questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic observability, safe auto-remediation, and IAM trust for SAP on EC2. 

## Key Concepts
- CloudWatch Logs integration for SAP trace data
- VPC Flow Logs for network visibility
- CloudWatch alarms + Lambda auto-remediation
- Safe-guards to avoid restart loops
- IAM role permissions for logs and EC2 commands

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  SAPRemediationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Path: '/'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPRemediation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                Resource: '*'
  SAPRemediationFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt SAPRemediationRole.Arn
      Runtime: nodejs14.x
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          const AWS = require('aws-sdk');
          exports.handler = async () => { console.log('Restart SAP HANA if needed'); };
  SAPHANA_CPU_Alarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: SAPHANA_CPU_Alarm
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/EC2
      Dimensions:
        - Name: InstanceId
          Value: !Ref SAPInstance
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 80
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !GetAtt SAPRemediationFunction.Arn
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to design immutable audit and backup pipelines across multi-account and multi-region SAP deployments, ensuring regulatory retention, tamper-evidence, and auditable disaster recovery tests.

## Key Concepts
- S3 Object Lock in Governance mode for SAP HANA backups
- Cross-region replication for DR bucket redundancy
- CloudTrail multi-region trails combined with OpenTelemetry exporting to a central data lake
- Cross-account KMS CMK grants with key rotation implications
- Least-privilege IAM roles and Service Control Policies (SCPs)
- DR validation and audit integrity verification procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  SapBackupsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub 'sap-backups-${AWS::AccountId}'
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      ObjectLockEnabled: true
      ObjectLockDefaultRetention:
        Mode: GOVERNANCE
        Days: 365
      BucketPolicy:
        PolicyText:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:
            - Sid: DenyDeleteWithGovernance
              Effect: Deny
              Principal: '*'
              Action: 's3:DeleteObject'
              Resource:
                - !Sub '${SapBackupsBucket.Arn}/*'
              Condition:
                StringNotEquals:
                  s3:SignatureAge: '3600000'
```

resource "aws_ssm_patch_baseline" "sap_hana_baseline" {
  name            = "sap-hana-patch-baseline-${var.environment}"

  operating_system = "SUSE_SLES"

}

Resources:

    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    Properties:
      Name: sap/prod/hana
      Description: "SAP HANA production credentials"
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username":"sapadm"}'
        GenerateStringKey: "password"
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\'
